title: Cases of EFL Secondary Students’ Prompt Engineering Pathways to Complete a Writing Task with ChatGPT
extended_summary:
This paper examines how a small group of secondary school English as a foreign language (EFL) students crafted prompts while using ChatGPT and other state-of-the-art chatbots to complete a blog-writing task. The central question is not whether the chatbot improved writing scores, but what kinds of prompt content students used and how their prompt sequences unfolded as they tried to get useful output from the tools.

The study is a qualitative case study of four high-achieving Form 1 students in a Hong Kong secondary school. Students completed the same timed writing task in a classroom after school, using iPads and the POE app, and their screen activity was recorded. The authors coded 36 valid prompt turns and identified six distinct prompt types, including auto-complete, search-engine style prompts, greetings, questions, natural-language instructions, and combined instruction-plus-example prompts. They also mapped each student’s pathway across chatbots to show how prompting evolved through trial-and-error.

The main conclusion is that students used a limited range of prompting strategies and did not receive explicit prompt-engineering instruction, suggesting they were experimenting rather than using a mature repertoire of techniques. The authors argue that prompt-engineering education could help EFL students use chatbots more effectively for writing tasks. The paper does not report subgroup outcome analyses for emergent readers, multilingual learners, students with disabilities, or other accessibility-related groups; any discussion of learner differences is speculative and not tied to comparative outcome data.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI's generative AI chatbot based on large language models, designed for conversational text generation and instruction following.
identified_tools.use_case: Used alongside other POE-hosted chatbots by secondary school EFL students to generate text while completing a blog-writing task; students experimented with prompts across chatbots, including ChatGPT.

quality_tier_rationale: This is a qualitative case study of four students’ prompt engineering pathways, not an experimental evaluation of learning outcomes. It provides descriptive evidence about chatbot use in EFL writing, but no comparative outcome data or subgroup analyses.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper suggests ChatGPT may support EFL writing and prompt-engineering learning, but it reports no effect sizes or measured impacts on literacy outcomes. Any subgroup-related comments are speculative and not supported by outcome data.
